meta.methodology: Read framework.md, then all edges from torahData.js with reference===97 (found 4 edges, all type 'eitza', zero bechina). Then read torah_97.txt in full. Systematically identified every occurrence of bechina language: בְּחִינַת, נִקְרֵאת/נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן, הַיְנוּ (used as an equation). Each concept so identified was checked: (1) does it appear as a node in the torahData.js dataset? (2) if it is in the dataset, is it assigned to a package? Since the dataset has no bechina edges for Torah #97, all identified concepts are gaps requiring new node additions to the dataset.

When prayer is properly conducted (with Menashe and Efraim), the taanug is revealed anew — God's delight is fulfilled. Gilad = gal-ed = revelation of this taanug. The taanug node IS what Gilad declares to be revealed. Belongs in Package 3.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 5 describes gadlut as one of the obstacles to prayer ('שֶׁעוֹמֵד לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּגַדְלוּת'). However, it is not declared a bechina — there is no 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' statement equating gadlut to a concept. It is mentioned as a cause of the block, not as a concept sharing nature with another. Excluded.

Line 5 mentions yichus as the content of what the person forgets via Menashe ('שֶׁהוּא מְיֻחָס גָּדוֹל'). Line 6 proof text says: 'כִּי נַשַּׁנִי אֱלֹקִים אֶת כָּל בֵּית אָבִי – זֶה הַיִּחוּס.' This is a gloss/explanation of the proof verse, not a bechina declaration. The Rebbe says 'zeh ha-yichus' — this verse illustrates yichus — but does not use bechina language to equate yichus to another concept. Excluded.

Line 6: 'וְאֶת כָּל עֲמָלִי – שֶׁעָמַל בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא.' This is the second thing to be forgotten (one's spiritual toil/accomplishments). It is an explanation of the verse, not a bechina statement. Excluded.

Line 2: 'יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לְמַעְלָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא אֶלְדָּד וּמֵידָד, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַשֶּׁפַע יוֹרֵד לָעוֹלָם.' Eldad-Medad is a place/source from which shefa descends. The Rebbe then breaks the name into letter-pairs (Alef-Lamed = dad; Mem-Yud = dad). The NAME Eldad-Medad is not itself declared a bechina in the standard sense — it is the Rebbe's source-reference that he immediately decomposes into the letter pairs. The letter pairs (א"ל and מ"י) are the actual bechina nodes; Eldad-Medad is the named heavenly place. Excluded as a separate node (already captured by the letter-pair analysis).

Foreign thoughts are mentioned multiple times (lines 7, 8) as what falls upon the person during prayer and what must be broken. But the Rebbe does not declare 'X הוא בְּחִינַת מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת' or vice versa. They are the content of the problem, not a bechina-labeled concept. Excluded.

Lines 7, 14: holy thoughts of prayer are what break the foreign thoughts and what is meant by 'מָעוֹז רֹאשִׁי.' But no bechina declaration. 'מָעוֹז רֹאשִׁי – הַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּגְבִּיר הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת' — this 'הַיְנוּ' is a verse interpretation, not a bechina equation between two concepts. Excluded.

Line 3: 'נַעֲשֶׂה מִן הֵא דָּלֶת, עַל־שֵׁם דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמַהּ כְּלוּם.' The Heh becomes a Dalet when shefa is withdrawn — the Dalet represents poverty/lack (dleit lah mi-garma klum = she has nothing of her own). This is part of the Heh/Dalet dynamic. The Dalet represents absence of shefa. It could be considered a negative state of the letter-Heh-as-shefa, but no explicit bechina declaration marks Dalet as equal to another concept. The framework emphasizes 'bechina statements' specifically. Excluded from the additions list but noted: if the dataset were to include it, it would be an evil/neutral counterpart in the letters domain, showing the ה becoming ד when the divine flow (shefa) withdraws.

analysis_notes.important_note: All 20 bechina-connected concepts in Torah #97 are gaps (not in the dataset as bechina edges for this Torah). The dataset needs 20 new nodes/edges added for Torah #97 bechina representation. The 4 existing eitza edges correctly classify eitza relationships (ענוה → יראה, Menashe+Efraim prayer → ענוה ושפלות, etc.) and should be retained.
analysis_notes.structural_observation: Torah #97 has no evil package. It is a positive teaching about how prayer attains sovereignty (memshala). The only negative element is the withdrawal of shefa (ה becoming ד) and the obstacles to prayer (gadlut before prayer, foreign thoughts during prayer), but these are mentioned in narrative/eitza context, not labeled as bechina concepts forming an evil cluster.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: ABSENT: No evil bechina cluster exists in Torah #97. The Rebbe does not develop an explicit evil counterpart. The obstacles (gadlut, machshavot zarot) are presented as problems to be overcome (eitza context), not as a parallel evil ontological domain with its own bechina structure.
